description: Our project focuses on leveraging NASA's open-source satellite data, Earth observation technologies, and Artificial Intelligence to solve real-world challenges. We aim to develop an innovative, data-driven solution that addresses environmental and societal problems. Through this hackathon, we aspire to transform space-based data into meaningful insights and impactful solutions for Earth.
summary: The NASA SPHEREx hackathon challenge focuses on developing a user-friendly web application to explore astronomical data collected by NASA's SPHEREx space telescope. The application should allow users to view real space images, explore different sky regions, switch between 102 infrared wavelengths, and compare observations taken on different dates. It should also highlight potential moving objects such as comets, asteroids, and stars, providing relevant information about their positions and properties. Using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and PHP, the project aims to transform complex NASA datasets into interactive visualizations, making space exploration accessible to everyone.
details:
# SPHEREx ChronoScope – Explore the Universe

SPHEREx ChronoScope is an interactive, web-based astronomy platform designed to help people explore the universe using multi-epoch sky observations. The project focuses on comparing astronomical images captured at different times to identify changes and investigate moving celestial objects such as asteroids, comets, and stars.

The platform allows users to search for celestial regions using coordinates or object names and compare observations through advanced techniques such as Blink Comparison, Image Subtraction, and Coaddition. It also provides features for exploring 102 infrared spectral bands, analysing light curves, investigating object movement, and viewing astronomical catalogue information.

The major benefits of this project include simplified astronomical data exploration, improved visual comparison, support for educational activities, and increased public interest in space science.

The project is developed using web technologies such as HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and React.js, with Python for backend development. Visual Studio Code is used as the development environment, and Render is used for deployment.

The creativity of our project lies in combining interactive visualisation, astronomical image comparison, infrared data exploration, and motion analysis into a single user-friendly platform.

During development, we considered usability, performance, data accuracy, accessibility, responsiveness, scalability, and scientific reliability.

Our ultimate goal is to make complex astronomical observations easier to explore and understand, encouraging students, researchers, and the public to participate in discovering the mysteries of the universe.
